readout_other: Western blotting (WRAP53, TERT, BDNF, PSD-95, APP, A-beta, Tau, p-Tau); telomere length qPCR (T/S ratio); Morris water maze; fear conditioning; open field; rotarod; c-Fos immunofluorescence; beta-galactosidase senescence staining; RNA-seq transcriptomics; 16S rRNA gut microbiota sequencing
direction_notes: UDBS significantly increased c-Fos expression (a neuronal activation marker) in the cortex and hippocampus of aging mice, and was associated with decelerated telomere shortening and improved cognitive and motor behaviour.

exposures.label: UDBS of hippocampus and cortex (normal, AD-model, and aging mice)

timing.protocol_description: UDBS delivered with 1 s sonication trains and a 1 s inter-stimulus interval, for 30 min/day. Experiment 1 (normal mice): treated for 14 days then sacrificed for telomerase western blotting. Experiment 2 (APP/PS1 Alzheimer's model mice): UDBS administered for 66 days, then behavioural testing and sacrifice for telomere evaluation on Day 100. Experiment 3 (aging mice): treated for 49 days, with behavioural, telomere, immunofluorescence and transcriptomic evaluation.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Experiment 1: Six normal mice were randomized into the sham $\left( n = 3 \right)$ and UDBS (n = 3) groups. The mice were treated for 14 days (30 min/day) and then sacrificed for western blotting of telomerase.

The three sub-experiments used different treatment durations (14, 66, and 49 days respectively), so a single session count cannot be given; durations are described in protocol_description.
